title: Observability dashboards + guardrail alerting for route-level A/B experiments
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Goal
Create first-class Grafana dashboards and alert rules for route-level A/B experiments, keyed by experiment_id (and variant_id where appropriate). Alerts must integrate with the operational guardrails + rollback workflow so SRE/oncall can quickly identify regressions and trigger rollback.

Background
Route-level A/B testing introduces a new high-risk routing primitive (intentional traffic shifting). We need consistent dashboards and actionable alerts so:
- customers/internal dogfood can compare variants on latency/cost/errors with confidence
- SRE can detect regressions quickly and execute rollback
- we avoid metric cardinality explosions from tagging experiment_id across hot paths

Scope
1) Dashboards (Grafana)
- Experiment overview (single experiment_id selector)
  - exposure volume (req/s) by variant
  - top-line latency (p50/p95/p99) by variant
  - TTFT (p50/p95) by variant for streaming endpoints
  - error rate breakdown (5xx, 4xx incl 429, timeouts)
  - cost attribution (tokens in/out, estimated GPU $ or Redwood cost units) by variant
  - “Guardrail status” panel (latest evaluation results from guardrail evaluator, plus rollback events)
- Drill-down panels
  - per-region comparison (region dimension, limited allowlist)
  - per-route comparison (route_id allowlisted / low-card only)
  - capacity signals where available (queueing/backpressure indicators) to explain 429 spikes

2) Alert rules
Alert rules should be experiment-aware and low-noise. Default thresholds align with guardrail policy doc.
- Latency regression guardrail (p95 and p99) on variant vs control
- TTFT regression guardrail (streaming endpoints)
- Error-rate regression guardrail (5xx, timeouts)
- 429 rate increase (capacity/quotas) by region to catch “variant routes to constrained capacity” incidents
- Exposure anomalies
  - exposure volume drops to ~0 for one variant (likely routing/config issue)
  - configured 50/50 but observed distribution deviates beyond tolerance (hashing/tagging bug detection; should be best-effort)
- Missing instrumentation / ingestion
  - exposure events absent for active experiment (pipeline or gateway regression)

3) Integration with rollback workflow
- Alerts must link directly to the runbook and to the experiment details page (Console deep link)
- Where guardrail evaluator is enabled, alerts should include the recommended action (pause/rollback) and whether auto-rollback fired
- Add an annotation/event stream for experiment lifecycle changes (start/stop/rollback) so graphs are interpretable

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Customer-configurable custom alert thresholds
- Per-customer bespoke dashboards (we ship a standard template)
- Full statistical significance UI (handled by results UI + aggregation layer)

Key design constraints
- Cardinality: experiment_id and variant_id are allowed; avoid adding user_id / api_key_id / arbitrary headers. Route should be route_id (normalized) not raw URL. Region is allowlisted.
- Data sources: use aggregated datasets/materialized views where possible; avoid Grafana querying raw high-volume event logs.
- Multi-region: dashboards must support filtering by region and still render if a subset of regions is missing data.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Grafana dashboard(s) merged into observability pack repo and deployed to staging
- [ ] Dashboard supports experiment_id selection and renders all core panels within acceptable query time (<= 5s typical)
- [ ] Alert rules defined with routing to #eng-sre and oncall page policy for P0 guardrails
- [ ] Alerts include links: runbook + Console experiment page + relevant graphs
- [ ] Annotations for experiment lifecycle events present on dashboards
- [ ] Verified in staging with dogfood experiment (at least one experiment_id) and one induced regression (synthetic or controlled)
- [ ] Documented “how to use dashboards during an incident” snippet added to runbook or linked in ticket

References
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/ab-testing-emergency-disable-and-rollback.json
- Guardrail policy: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/ab-testing-slo-and-guardrail-policy.json
- Metrics schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/ab-testing-metrics-schema-v1.json
- Related implementation PRs
  - Guardrail evaluator + auto-rollback hook: sources/github/redwood/pr_18459_guardrail-evaluator-and-auto-rollback-hook.json
  - Latency metrics by experiment: sources/github/redwood/pr_18415_latency-metrics-by-experiment.json
  - Cost attribution by variant: sources/github/redwood/pr_18403_cost-attribution-by-variant.json
  - Reduce metric cardinality experiment tags: sources/github/redwood/pr_18519_reduce-metric-cardinality-experiment-tags.json

Open questions
- Alert ownership: page SRE oncall vs route to #eng-sre only during beta? (Proposed: page oncall for P0 guardrails only when experiment is in “Running” state and traffic_split >= 10% to variant.)
- Control definition: do we assume variant A is control always, or use explicit control_variant_id from experiment config? (Preferred: explicit.)
- Cost panel: use Redwood cost units (metering) vs GPU $ estimate? (Preferred: Redwood cost units for consistency with billing; add optional panel for GPU estimate if available.)
comments: 2026-02-07 (Sean Gallagher): For beta, we need at minimum: p95 latency regression alert + 5xx/timeouts alert + 429-by-region alert, all keyed by experiment_id. Please link alerts to the rollback runbook and include the Console deep link so Support can coordinate with customers quickly.

2026-02-09 (Logan Wright): Metrics tags are finalized in schema v1. Please do not add route as a free-form label; use route_id only and keep it behind an allowlist. If you need additional dims for debugging, we should do it via logs/traces, not metrics.

2026-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Started dashboard mock in staging Grafana. Query performance is OK using the ENG-2844 rollups; raw exposure event queries were too slow. Next step is annotations for experiment lifecycle events (start/stop/rollback).

2026-02-14 (Allison Grant): Please add a “data freshness” panel (last_ingest_timestamp) so we can distinguish routing issues from pipeline lag. We’ve been burned by silent ingestion delays on other features.

2026-02-18 (Aisha Bello): Implemented alert prototypes with experiment state gating (only fire if running=true). Need a reliable source-of-truth for running state in metrics; otherwise we’ll maintain a small mapping in alert config generated from control plane export.

2026-02-20 (Miles Thornton): For multi-region reliability, add an alert for regional skew (variant B only failing in eu-west) that doesn’t require high-cardinality breakdowns. A simple per-region error-rate panel is enough; alerting can be limited to ‘any region > threshold’ during beta.

2026-02-22 (Aisha Bello): Added annotations via audit log export (start/stop/rollback events) into Grafana annotations datasource. Verified with a test experiment in staging; rollback is clearly visible on graphs.

2026-02-24 (Sean Gallagher): Looks good. One request before we call it done: make the alert payload include experiment_name (not just ID) so oncall can recognize it quickly. If that’s not available in metrics, add it as an annotation/label in the alert message via lookup table from control plane export.
activity: 2026-02-06: Ticket created; aligned scope with SRE guardrail requirements for beta.

2026-02-18: Alerting rules drafted; added gating on experiment running state to reduce noise.
2026-02-22: Added lifecycle annotations (start/stop/rollback) and validated with staging dogfood.
2026-02-24: PR opened in observability pack repo; pending final review from SRE on alert routing and payload fields.
